target_customer: Renters and property managers or leasing platforms that embed pay-over-time financing for move-in and lease costs
problem: Renters tie up $1K or more in deposits and move-in costs, and properties carry bad debt and lost income when price blocks a lease.
business_model: Embedded BNPL for moving and renting sold through a widget, API or property management software integration

founders.name: Jason Corwin
previous_startups: TellFi (YC W11, inactive per YC listing)
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page; also described as a former volunteer firefighter.

founders.name: Roland Mansilla
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built a stablecoin product and helped launch a credit platform that originated over $120M in under 12 months. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Embedding installment lending needs underwriting, a lending or capital partner and integrations with property management systems, though the front end widget is simple. The sources do not describe the stack.

defensibility.rationale: No stated proprietary data or regulatory position in the sources. Embedded financing partnerships with property managers could create some switching cost but none is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A 2026 article notes Affirm piloted splitting rent into two installments with Esusu. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Safely Finance.

market_need_then: The company's own pitch states most renters lock up $1K or more in deposits. No dated 2019 demand evidence was found in the sources opened.

branding.domain_note: Used safelyfinance.co, not a .com. The domain is now a parked page that says it may be for sale (checked 2026).

brand_strength.rationale: No press, merch or community evidence found. The name is close to other Safely-named companies, including Safely Deposit and an unrelated renovation lender, which makes it easy to confuse.

outcome_analysis: The company is listed Inactive by YC with a two person team, and the only funding found is a reported $500K convertible note from early 2019 in one database. No shutdown announcement, post-mortem or press coverage was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are asserted. The company's domain is now parked and for sale, and a failure tracker lists an end year of 2022 with unverified figures.
notes: Funding rests on a single database (CB Insights, $500K, convertible note, dated 2019-01, investors Y Combinator and Tribe Capital). Another failure-analysis tracker lists about $4.0M burned and an end year of 2022, unverified and not recorded as a round. Product Hunt shows a launch dated 2021-10-19. The YC page ties Corwin to Safely Deposit while another profile names Mansilla; unresolved. Competitors left empty because only undated pages (CB Insights compare pages, Product Hunt alternatives) were found. Exit type is unknown because YC says Inactive but no source gives a date or cause. An unrelated Safely Finance home-renovation lender exists and was excluded.
